mainProgression.description: The purest possible I-IV-V folk progression. Three chords form the backbone of the entire song, demonstrating that harmonic simplicity can carry profound lyrical content. One of the most important folk songs ever written.

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Stable, warm tonic that grounds each musical phrase
C (IV) - Subdominant providing gentle motion and the sense of a musical 'question'
D (V) - Dominant that creates forward momentum and urgency before resolving to G

techniques.name: Folk Strumming Pattern
techniques.description: Steady, rhythmic folk strumming with a moderate tempo, emphasizing downbeats and a flowing down-up pattern that supports the vocal storytelling

notes: G: 320003 - full open G chord shape
C: X32010 - standard open C chord
D: XX0232 - standard open D chord
Use a basic down-down-up-up-down-up strumming pattern
Accent the first downbeat of each measure for rhythmic clarity
Keep the wrist loose for a natural, flowing folk feel
sequence: Strum G for the first half of the question line
Move to C for the second half of the question line
Return to G and repeat for the next question line
D chord appears at the end of the third question for tension
Refrain starts on C, moves to D, resolves to G
tips: Strum gently - folk music calls for a warm, unforced sound
Use a thin pick or fingerstrum for a softer, warmer tone
Let the chords ring between changes for a full sound
Listen to Dylan's recording to internalize the easy, rolling rhythm
details.progression: G - C - D (the fundamental I-IV-V folk pattern)

techniques.name: Harmonica-Style Guitar Fills (Optional)
techniques.description: Simple single-note fills between vocal lines that emulate Dylan's harmonica breaks, played on the upper strings in G major pentatonic

notes: Based on G major pentatonic scale on the B and high E strings
Fill the gaps between vocal phrases with 2-3 note melodic fragments
Use a harmonica rack to play actual harmonica while strumming for the authentic Dylan experience
Can be omitted entirely without affecting the song
sequence: During gaps between vocal phrases, pick 2-3 notes from G major pentatonic
Return to strumming before the next vocal phrase enters
Keep fills simple and brief - less is more
In harmonica breaks, the guitar just strums while harmonica leads
tips: Focus on mastering the strumming and singing first
If adding guitar fills, keep them simple and brief
A harmonica in the key of C (cross-harp in G) matches Dylan's approach
Less is more - the song's power is in the words, not instrumental flash
details.progression: G - C - D with pentatonic fills between vocal phrases

techniques.name: Three-Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Smooth transitions between the three most fundamental open chords in guitar playing: G, C, and D major

notes: G to C: Pivot on the ring finger from 3rd fret low E to 3rd fret A, shift index and middle
C to D: Lift from C shape and reform D on the top three strings
D to G: Largest jump - practice this transition the most
G and C share the ring finger on the 3rd fret (different strings)
These three transitions are the foundation of thousands of songs
sequence: Practice G to C transition 20 times slowly
Practice C to D transition 20 times slowly
Practice D to G transition 20 times slowly
Chain all three: G - C - D - G in a slow loop
Add the strumming pattern once transitions are smooth
tips: Keep fingers close to the fretboard during transitions
Visualize the next chord shape before you move
The moderate 90 BPM tempo is very forgiving for chord changes
These three chords will unlock hundreds of songs
details.progression: G - C - D fundamental transition practice

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Brief guitar intro establishing the key and gentle tempo with a few bars of the G chord
notes: Simple strumming on G to establish the key
Very short - just a bar or two before the vocal enters
Sets the gentle, contemplative mood
Some versions start with a harmonica intro instead

sections.name: Verse (Question Lines)
sections.description: The three question lines of the verse, with the vocal riding the G-C oscillation and D creating tension before the refrain
sections.progression: G - C - G - C - G - C - D
notes: Three question lines each oscillating between G and C
D chord appears at the end of the third line for harmonic tension
Strumming remains steady and supportive under the vocal
Each line follows the same G-C pattern for hypnotic repetition

sections.name: Refrain (The Answer)
sections.description: The iconic 'The answer, my friend, is blowinthe signature refrain resolving the musical and lyrical tension
sections.progression: C - D - G - C - G - C - D - G
notes: Starts on C (IV) for harmonic lift above the tonic
D (V) creates forward momentum toward resolution
Resolves to G (I) on the word 'wind' for emotional completion
The refrain is the emotional and musical resolution of each verse

sections.name: Harmonica Break
sections.description: Instrumental harmonica break over the verse progression where the guitar continues steady strumming as accompaniment
sections.progression: G - C - G - C - G - C - D
notes: Guitar continues the same strumming pattern underneath
Harmonica takes the melodic role over the verse changes
If playing solo guitar, can add simple fills or just strum through
Provides a breathing space between verses

sections.name: Final Refrain and Outro
sections.description: Final statement of the iconic vocal hook in the wind' followed by harmonica outro, resolving gently on the G chord
notes: Final statement of the answer refrain
Harmonica plays out over repeated progression
Song ends with a gentle resolve on G
No fade-out - clean, simple ending

beginner.focus: Learn the three fundamental open chords G, C, D and a basic folk strumming pattern
steps: Learn open G, C, and D chord shapes individually
Practice switching between G and C smoothly
Practice switching between C and D smoothly
Learn a basic folk strumming pattern (down-down-up-up-down-up)

intermediate.focus: Play through the complete song structure with vocals and proper phrasing
steps: Memorize the full song structure (verse-refrain-harmonica break pattern)
Practice singing the melody while strumming
Work on phrasing - matching strumming emphasis to lyrical accents
Add dynamics between verses and refrains

advanced.focus: Add harmonica accompaniment and develop a complete one-person performance
steps: Learn basic cross-harp harmonica in G (C harmonica)
Use a harmonica rack to play both guitar and harmonica simultaneously
Develop instrumental fills between vocal lines
Play along with Dylan's original recording for feel and timing
advanced.timeEstimate: 3-5 weeks for polished performance with harmonica

commonMistakes: Overcomplicating the strumming - keep it simple and steady like Dylan
Strumming too hard - folk music requires a gentle, even touch
Not counting bars properly - each question line has a specific chord rhythm
Rushing through the refrain instead of letting the resolution breathe
practiceRoutine: Warm up with G-C-D chord changes for 3-5 minutes
Practice the verse progression (G-C-G-C-G-C-D) slowly with a metronome
Practice the refrain progression (C-D-G) to ingrain the resolution
Play through the full three-verse structure without stopping
Add singing once the strumming is automatic
focusAreas: Clean and relaxed chord changes at 90 BPM
Steady folk strumming rhythm without rushing or dragging
metronomeWork: Start chord changes at 60 BPM to build accuracy
Gradually increase by 5 BPM increments to 90 BPM (song tempo)
Practice the full verse progression with metronome on beats 1 and 3
Play through complete song at tempo for consistency
